subject.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API

question: Should `after_compaction` expose a public `ctx.api.resetSession` contract, and should that contract permanently support explicit session-key compatibility calls?
rationale: This creates a compatibility-sensitive plugin API and preserves an external legacy calling form that is not established as a shipped OpenClaw contract; code review cannot choose that permanent SDK direction safely.

options.title: Reason-only scoped API
options.body: Expose only `resetSession("new" | "reset")`, bind it to the hook context session, and migrate the known consumer to the canonical form.

options.title: Keep legacy key overload
options.body: Document and test both forms as supported public API while continuing to reject keys other than the current hook session.

options.title: Do not add core API
options.body: Keep reset ownership outside the hook contract and require the integration to use an existing owner-specific lifecycle path.

recommendation.title: Reason-only scoped API
recommendation.body: Expose only `resetSession("new" | "reset")`, bind it to the hook context session, and migrate the known consumer to the canonical form.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal covers compaction, memory-flush, session persistence, and embedded runtime ownership across the affected paths.
